headline: High: shared broad network egress and overlapping data handling create leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection is lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared filesystem or message bus is documented, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, Firecrawl’s MCP-compatible client support and Chatwoot’s integrations create a plausible manual or tool-mediated bridge if outputs are copied between them. The pathway is weaker than data leakage because the profiles do not show default ingestion of each other’s outputs.
conditions: IF outputs from Firecrawl are copied into Chatwoot conversations or notes
IF an MCP or clipboard bridge is added between the two agents
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw scraped content into support workflows
Use a provenance tag on imported content
Restrict Chatwoot macros from executing pasted instructions
requires-engineering: add content sanitization before ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, messages, and reports, while Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys and has broad network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or operator context, sensitive customer data can be exposed to Firecrawl’s outbound requests or scraped content can be reintroduced into Chatwoot outputs.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports customer records into a shared workspace
IF Firecrawl is run on files containing customer data or API keys
IF either agent forwards its context to a third-party endpoint
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Remove secrets before sending content to Firecrawl
Use a redaction step on Chatwoot exports
Limit Firecrawl jobs to non-sensitive URLs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent network and file isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to mutable external resources through APIs and broad network egress, and Firecrawl explicitly supports multiple instances. Chatwoot also integrates with Slack, Shopify, and Linear, so overlapping writes are plausible if both are pointed at the same downstream system. The profiles do not prove shared locks or shared mutable targets, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same Slack, Shopify, or Linear workspace
IF Firecrawl instances operate concurrently on the same mutable target
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
Avoid shared write targets
Stagger jobs to reduce concurrent writes
Review downstream webhook destinations
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer-facing support content, and Firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data. If Firecrawl output is treated as authoritative and then inserted into Chatwoot workflows without verification, errors or malicious content can cascade into customer communications. The profiles show no built-in verification boundary, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is pasted into Chatwoot replies or macros
IF Chatwoot agents rely on scraped content without human review
mitigations: Require human review before sending customer replies
Mark scraped content as untrusted
Use a citation/verification checklist
Limit Firecrawl output to internal drafts
requires-engineering: add validation gates between scrape and support actions

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Firecrawl handles web content, screenshots, and API keys with broad network egress. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch is not proven; however, if regulated customer data is routed through Firecrawl, retention and transfer obligations can diverge. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Chatwoot is sent to Firecrawl
IF either agent retains screenshots or scraped pages beyond policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to Firecrawl
Block regulated records from scraping workflows
Document retention settings for both tools
Review vendor DPAs and residency claims
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
